svg.title: The closed world: what costs a major version and what does not
svg.desc: Version one of the format is a closed world, so changes fall into three groups. A major version is required for a new top-level field, a new field on a section, a new section key or a rename or a reorder, a fifth section status, a twelfth provenance label, a change to what an existing field means, or making an optional field required. A minor release, which still moves the document's version, covers raising a bound; bounds go up and never down inside a major line, and a reader must add the new version to the set it supports before it will read a document that uses the new headroom. Nothing moves the document's version for a new observation kind, for wording in the extraction recipe, which carries its own semver, for a new implementation release, or for editorial specification work. The compatibility contract runs backward only: a later reader accepts every valid earlier document in the line, and an earlier reader refuses a later document on the version, before shape.
svg.text: The closed world
A file you save today stays readable. What costs a major version, what moves the document's version, and what moves nothing: the cost has a step in it, and the step is publication.
Requires a major version
2.0, and nothing less
a new top-level field
a new field on a section
a new section key, a rename, a reorder
a fifth section status
a twelfth provenance label
a change to what an existing field means
making an optional field required
Every reader already built refuses these,
correctly. That is what it was told to do.
Moves the version
a minor release
raising a bound
Bounds go up and never down: lowering
one would invalidate documents that
were valid when they were written.
A reader supports exact versions. There
is no "any 1.x is fine" rule, so a reader
adds the new version to the set it
supports before it will read a document
that uses the new headroom.
Moves no version at all
the document format is unchanged
a new observation kind
not a specification change at all: the format
already says a reader ignores what it does
not recognise and carries it forward
wording in the extraction recipe
its own semver, recorded as source.recipeVersion
a new implementation release
a new SDK, a bug fix, a faster scanner
editorial specification work
new prose, new fixtures, a corrected example
Why it is closed
A reader refuses an unknown top-level field, an unknown field on a section, a section key outside the seventeen, a status outside the four, and a
provenance label outside the eleven. Refusing is the instruction, not a limitation: a reader that quietly dropped what it did not understand would
produce a handover that looks complete and is not, which is the exact failure the format exists to prevent.
Backward, required: a later reader accepts every valid earlier document in the line, and lists every earlier version in the set it supports.
Forward, none: an earlier reader refuses a later document on the version, before shape, because it cannot know what the later version added.
